Scenario: Release-readiness review of keyboard activation and assistive-technology evidence
Observed behaviour: The local browser harness focused the skip link but did not activate it using its synthetic Enter event; pointer activation moved focus to main#prototype-content.
Expected behaviour: Physical-keyboard activation and assistive-technology behaviour must be verified before a release decision.
Clinical or operational impact: No unsafe workflow progression was observed, but the required accessibility release evidence is incomplete and keyboard/assistive-technology conformance cannot be claimed.
Root-cause hypothesis: The automated browser harness did not faithfully reproduce physical-keyboard activation; no product root cause has been established.
Workaround: Do not approve a release or accessibility claim; retain the visible pointer-safe route only as observed browser evidence.
Fix: Execute physical-keyboard skip-link activation and a proportionate assistive-technology check, then record the observed result.
Retest result: Pass: Product Owner reported successful physical-keyboard and assistive-technology checks with no issue observed.
Release decision: Conditional Go — structured synthetic review only

Scenario: Product Owner visual review of the Sprint 6B prototype
Interaction state: Header, task context, evidence preview, workflow status, role navigation and portfolio walkthrough
Observed behaviour: Build-control and interviewer-facing explanations were visually prominent; workflow status was repeated before primary task content; the report preview was right-aligned; prototype navigation opened an interrupting role-handoff dialog; several screens provided no obvious portfolio continuation; and SCR-10 highlighted the wrong journey stage.
Expected behaviour: User-facing screens should lead with the represented user task and evidence, show the represented role non-intrusively, keep status and ownership secondary, expose an explicit next walkthrough control after successful local actions, and visually separate portfolio navigation without changing workflow behaviour or authority.
Clinical or operational impact: The defect did not bypass a clinical or operational control, but it materially reduced comprehension and could cause a reviewer to misunderstand the product flow, role authority and next action.
Root-cause hypothesis: Sprint 6B presentation controls accumulated as equal-priority explanatory elements instead of one task-first hierarchy, and the shared journey mapping covered only one confirmation phase label.
Workaround: Use readable hash routes while the correction is applied; do not infer workflow progression from screen navigation.
Fix: Reworked the shared header, role treatment, task hierarchy, source-report dialog, journey rail, status placement, referral checklist and separate portfolio navigation; removed the rendered role-handoff popup; added explicit post-action walkthrough controls; preserved controllers, fixtures, routes, human authority and AI boundaries.
Retest result: Pass: TypeScript lint passed; all 72 Node tests passed; Vite production build passed; browser checks passed on launch, result review, referral handoff, report preview, confirmation and 390px responsive layout.
Release decision: No release decision changed; final QLT-6B-02 whole-prototype regression remains required.

Scenario: Product Owner visual review of the activity-trace header
Observed behaviour: The activity-trace header displayed `Synthetic operational or governance reviewer` immediately above `Operational or governance reviewer`, repeating the same role.
Expected behaviour: When a synthetic display name normalises to the represented role, the header should show the canonical role once while retaining the viewing-mode and synthetic-data labels.
Clinical or operational impact: No workflow, authority or safety control was affected; the repetition reduced header clarity and made the prototype appear unfinished.
Root-cause hypothesis: The shared session header always rendered both display name and role without checking whether the display name was only the role prefixed by `Synthetic`.
Workaround: None required; the activity trace remained read-only and usable.
Fix: Added shared normalisation that suppresses only an exact repeated role and retains distinct name/role combinations; initials now derive from the displayed identity.
Retest result: Pass: focused regression test passed; TypeScript lint passed; all 73 Node tests passed; Vite production build passed; browser inspection showed one `Operational or governance reviewer` label and no secondary repeated role.
Release decision: No release decision changed; final QLT-6B-02 whole-prototype regression remains required.

Scenario: Product Owner visual review of synthetic labels and pre-launch identity
Interaction state: Global header, launch and episode overview
Observed behaviour: The screen repeated synthetic-data wording in the portfolio disclaimer, role badge, person/case labels and coordinator label. Before access, the header also presented a signed-in state whose text said that no session existed.
Expected behaviour: A single global portfolio-data disclaimer should identify the prototype; screen content should use the represented role and case terms without duplicate labels. Before access, the header should describe the access preview rather than a signed-in session.
Clinical or operational impact: No workflow, authority or safety control was affected, but repeated labels and a contradictory session statement reduced credibility and could mislead a portfolio reviewer.
Root-cause hypothesis: The synthetic fixture marker was rendered independently in the shell, session card and screen content, while the pre-launch shell reused signed-in presentation markup.
Workaround: The affected screens remained available; no workflow action was recorded.
Fix: Removed the per-role badge and repeated visible labels, replaced the pre-launch signed-in treatment with a truthful access preview, kept one global `Portfolio prototype · synthetic data only` disclaimer, and relabelled the report modal as a read-only demonstration document.
Retest result: Pass: focused shell, orientation and evidence-preview tests passed; TypeScript lint passed; all 73 Node tests passed; Vite production build passed; browser inspection of launch and overview found only the global portfolio-data disclaimer and no false signed-in state.
Release decision: No release decision changed; final QLT-6B-02 whole-prototype regression remains required.
